mechanism_narrative: A lower current federal funds rate level is associated with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days, as lower rates reduce the discount rate for equity valuation.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 4.5%, it signals a restrictive monetary policy that increases discount rates and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 40% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 4.5%.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous expansion in housing starts and retail sales signals robust consumer demand, which drives corporate earnings growth and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint signal of rising HOUST and RSAFS fails to produce positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: In periods of high unemployment (UNRATE > 6.0%), the S&P 500 tends to rise as investors anticipate central bank stimulus and economic recovery, leading to positive forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of instances when UNRATE > 6.0%.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production below 105.0 (current value 111.84) signals economic weakness that reduces near-term corporate earnings expectations, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 40% of instances when INDPRO < 105.0.

mechanism_narrative: A higher quarterly GDP growth rate (GDPC1) is associated with stronger corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days, as the economy expands.
failure_condition: The correlation between GDPC1 and 60-day SPX returns is negative or insignificant (p>0.05) over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly payroll gain exceeding 138,000 jobs signals strong labor market conditions that may lead to inflationary pressures, prompting the Federal Reserve to tighten policy and causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 40% of instances when PAYEMS > 138000.0.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly CPI reading above 220.0 indicates accelerating inflation, which may prompt the Federal Reserve to raise rates, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 40% of instances when CPIAUCSL > 220.0.
